One of the strengths of the course was that expectations were communicated early. Before the semester began, the instructor mentioned that the exams would be more challenging than the homework and the material covered in class. While this transparency was appreciated, the course did not sufficiently prepare students for that level of difficulty. Although the theoretical content was covered, there was a lack of challenging, exam-style problems discussed during lectures that would help bridge the gap between class material and assessments.

A major weakness of the course was the limited number of problems solved in class. Structure is a subject that heavily relies on practice, and solving more problems step-by-step during lectures would have been very beneficial. Additionally, encouraging students to come up to the board and actively participate in problem-solving could have increased engagement and improved understanding.

Furthermore, no past papers, mock exams, or sample exam-format questions were provided. In other technical courses such as physics or mathematics, these resources help students understand the structure, expectations, and difficulty of exams. The absence of such materials made exam preparation more difficult and unclear.
